projects.title: A home, rebuilt
projects.summary: A mother and her children were living in a makeshift hut of sticks, sacks and scraps. Today they sleep behind solid walls and a locked door.
story: For years, home for this family was a small makeshift hut, its frame of bent sticks patched with sacks, tarpaulin and whatever cloth and scrap could be found. In the dry season it trapped the heat; when the rains came, nothing kept them out.

Ahlul Kheir Foundation mobilised contributions from the community and built the family a permanent home: plastered walls, an iron-sheet roof, proper doors and a shaded veranda where the children now sit together.
This is what our shelter programme exists for. We do not hand out tents and leave. We stay until a family has a home that will last.

projects.title: Mama Halima’s family
projects.summary: Nine children, a newborn in her arms, and a grass hut with nothing to cook. “Please support me with whatever Allah has blessed you with.”
story: We were told about a family who were struggling badly, so our team went to find them. We found Halima Ahmed outside a grass hut, holding her newborn baby, with her children gathered around her.

Halima has nine children and had only just given birth. Their father has no work. One of her children is sick and does not have enough blood. Inside the hut there was nothing to cook with. As our team put it, “they cannot even light a fire to cook food.”

“I’m really struggling,” Halima told us, “and it’s only Allah who can take away my struggles. My brothers and sisters, I have a lot of problems. Please support me with whatever Allah has blessed you with. Help me, help me.”

That day our volunteers unpacked food supplies for the family. We want to keep helping Halima and her children with whatever Allah provides through you. Watch her story in her own words, then give if you can.

projects.title: Ramadan 2027 Food Appeal
projects.summary: Every Ramadan, families who fast all day have little to break their fast with. Thirty dollars changes that for a whole month.
story: Each year our Ramadan food packs carry the basics a family needs for the month: rice, lentils, flour, cooking oil and dates. We pack them by hand, then deliver them to the households that need them most.
As little as $30 is enough to feed an entire family for the whole of Ramadan. Pledge now so we can buy in bulk before prices rise and have every pack ready before the first fast.
“Whoever provides food for a fasting person to break their fast will have a reward like theirs, without anything being taken from the reward of the fasting person.” (Tirmidhi)

projects.title: Ramadan Food Distribution 2025
projects.summary: Sponsored by Jamia Mosque Nairobi and distributed by Ahlul Kheir Foundation: a full month of food for families observing Ramadan.
story: In Ramadan 2025 we again partnered with Jamia Mosque Nairobi to bring dry-food packs to struggling households. Volunteers packed sacks of rice, flour and sugar, and topped each with a jerrycan of cooking oil.
Families came to collect their packs, and the courtyard filled with rows of sacks waiting for their owners.
The yellow jerrycans in these photographs have become a symbol of the season for us. Each one marks a family that broke its fast with dignity.

projects.title: Dry Food Distribution, Ramadhan 2021
projects.summary: Our first large Ramadan programme with Jamia Mosque Nairobi, delivered by the Ahlul Kheir Women Group across several villages.
story: Before we were a registered NGO, we were the Ahlul Kheir Women Group, and Ramadan 2021 was one of our biggest efforts yet. Sponsored by Jamia Mosque Nairobi, we distributed dry-food packages across several communities.
Under acacia trees and beside village walls, families received flour, rice, sugar and cooking oil.
It proved what a small group of committed women could organise, and it set the pattern for every Ramadan since.

projects.title: Emergency Water Trucking
projects.summary: When the rains fail and wells run dry, our clean-water tankers reach families before thirst turns into crisis.
story: In the worst droughts, women and children walk for hours in search of water, and what they find is often unsafe. Our Emergency Water Trucking Initiative brings clean water directly to the villages that need it most.
When the tanker arrives, the queue of yellow jerrycans stretches across the plain. Every container filled means a family can cook, drink and wash without risking illness.
We have invested in water tanker trucks so we can respond quickly when severe droughts or other disasters strike.

projects.title: Shallow Wells
projects.summary: Each shallow well we dig serves up to 400 people. We have dug at least four in the past three years.
story: Water trucking saves lives in an emergency. A well changes a village for a generation.
Ahlul Kheir Foundation has dug no fewer than four shallow wells across drought-prone areas in the past three years. Each one can support up to 400 people with a steady, sustainable source of water.
The work is hard and the ground is rocky. Once a well is lined and capped, though, mothers no longer spend their mornings walking for water, and children have time for school.

projects.title: Eid al-Adha Qurbani
projects.summary: Your qurbani, shared with families who might not otherwise taste meat all year.
story: Every Eid al-Adha we carry out qurbani on behalf of donors and share the meat with families in need, or gift live goats so a family can benefit for longer.
For pastoralist households that have lost their herds to drought, a single goat can mean milk for the children and the beginning of a new flock.

projects.title: Madrasa & Qur’anic School
projects.summary: Integrated madrasa education and graduation ceremonies that celebrate every child who completes their studies.
story: Our integrated madrasa and Qur’anic school gives children a strong foundation in faith alongside their everyday education.

Graduation day is one of the proudest days of our year. Students in white robes, girls receiving their certificates, families who have sacrificed so their children could learn: these are the moments that remind us why we began.
Your support helps pay for teachers, learning materials and a good place to learn.

projects.title: Building for the Community
projects.summary: From family homes to community buildings: safe, lasting structures where they are needed most.
story: Construction is one of the most lasting things we do. We build safe homes for vulnerable families and respond quickly with shelter after disasters.
Our long-term objectives include rehabilitating social infrastructure (schools, wells, dams, hospitals and mosques) in partnership with local communities.

projects.title: Care at the Doorstep
projects.summary: Food parcels, mobility aids and a kind visit for the people who cannot come to us: elders, the sick, and children with disabilities.
story: Not everyone can stand in a queue. Our volunteers travel to homes deep in the bush to deliver food, blankets and essentials directly to the people who need them most.
Among them was a young girl who could not walk. She received her own wheelchair, and with it the freedom to move.
These visits are quiet work and rarely photographed, yet they are at the heart of who we are.

projects.title: Project Mzee Hache
projects.summary: Caring for an elder with dignity: cleaning and dressing wounds, new clothes, and a team that kept coming back.
story: “Mzee” is how we honour an elder in Kiswahili. Project Mzee Hache was about restoring dignity to one of them.
Our volunteers cleaned and treated his wounds, washed and dressed him in fresh clothes, and brought food and supplies to his home.
Watch the film to see the care our team gave him.

projects.title: Community Clean-Up
projects.summary: Gloves on, sacks out: our volunteers cleared dumping sites and roadsides, filling a truck with waste.
story: Protecting the environment is part of our mission. Plastic waste chokes the bush, harms livestock and breeds disease.
Our volunteers in high-visibility vests spent the day clearing dumping sites, collecting plastic and loading a truck to haul it away.
Clean streets are healthier streets, and every clean-up shows the community what we can achieve together.

projects.title: Official Launch, August 2025
projects.summary: Ten years after a group of women began with almost nothing, Ahlul Kheir Foundation was formally launched as a registered NGO.
story: On 22 August 2025 we gathered friends, partners and supporters to formally launch Ahlul Kheir Foundation. The programme included Qur’an recitation, the founder’s speech, a presentation of our work and impact, and testimonials from guests.
At its centre stood our NGO Certificate of Registration, tied with a red ribbon: the moment a community group became a registered organisation.
We are grateful to everyone who stood with us. This is only the beginning.
